faqs.question: What are the industrial uses of MEG (monoethylene glycol) in Oman?
faqs.answer: Monoethylene glycol (MEG, ethylene glycol, CAS 107-21-1) has three major industrial applications in Oman. First, as a gas hydrate inhibitor: MEG is injected into oil and gas pipelines and wellheads in Oman's upstream oil and gas sector to prevent gas hydrate formation in high-pressure, low-temperature flow lines — it is the preferred glycol for large-scale hydrate inhibition because of its lower molecular weight and lower viscosity. Second, as an antifreeze and coolant: MEG-water mixtures (30–50% MEG) protect vehicle and industrial cooling systems against freezing and overheating; in Oman's hot climate, MEG coolant extends water boiling point from 100°C to over 107°C, protecting modern high-performance engines. Third, as a PET resin feedstock: MEG reacts with terephthalic acid (PTA) to produce polyethylene terephthalate (PET) used in bottles, packaging, and polyester fibres. Global Chemicals LLC supplies technical-grade and industrial-grade MEG for all these Oman applications.

faqs.question: What is the correct MEG to water ratio for industrial cooling system antifreeze in Oman?
faqs.answer: For industrial cooling systems in Oman, a MEG-water mixture of 30–40% MEG by volume provides adequate protection against freezing and raises the boiling point of the coolant. Pure water boils at 100°C at sea level; a 40% MEG mixture raises the boiling point to approximately 104°C and provides freeze protection to −24°C — more than adequate for Oman's climate where freezing is not a concern. The benefit of MEG antifreeze in Oman is boiling point elevation and corrosion inhibition rather than freeze protection. A properly inhibited MEG coolant protects aluminium, steel, copper, and cast iron components from corrosion, cavitation, and scale formation, extending cooling system life compared to plain water. Higher MEG concentrations (above 60%) actually reduce heat transfer efficiency and increase viscosity without benefit in Oman conditions. Automotive MEG antifreeze products include corrosion inhibitor packages; industrial MEG for process cooling systems requires separate inhibitor addition. Global Chemicals LLC supplies MEG with inhibitor recommendations.

title: DEG (Diethylene Glycol) — Resin & Plasticiser Grade
description: Diethylene glycol ≥99.5% for polyester resins, plasticisers, and natural-gas dehydration blend make-up in Oman & GCC.

details.longDescription:
Diethylene glycol (DEG, 2,2'-oxydiethanol, diglycol, C4H10O3, CAS 111-46-6) is a clear, colourless, nearly odourless and hygroscopic liquid supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in resin and plasticiser grade at 99.5% minimum purity by GC, with water at 0.1% maximum by Karl Fischer, colour at 10 APHA maximum, density 1.118 g/cm³ at 20 °C and boiling point 244–245 °C. It is packed in 235 kg drums, 1,000 L IBCs and bulk from stock in Muscat. DEG sits between MEG and TEG in the ethylene glycol series.

Resins and polymers: DEG is one of the glycols condensed with maleic and phthalic anhydride to make unsaturated polyester resins, where its ether link gives a more flexible, tougher cured resin than propylene glycol alone. It is a building block for polyester polyols used in polyurethane foams, coatings and elastomers, and reacts with benzoic acid to give diethylene glycol dibenzoate, a plasticiser for PVC and adhesives. It is also a raw material for morpholine and other intermediates.

Solvent and humectant: DEG dissolves dyes, resins and nitrocellulose and holds moisture, so it is used in printing inks, textile lubricants and conditioning agents, and as a component of cement grinding aids. For natural-gas dehydration and hydrate inhibition, see the MEG versus DEG guide linked on this page. DEG is an industrial chemical only. It has caused repeated mass poisonings, with many child victims, when substituted for glycerine or propylene glycol in medicines such as cough syrups, and it has been found in counterfeit toothpaste; it must never be used in food, beverages, medicines, toothpaste or cosmetics. We supply against end-use declarations where destination import rules require them.

Handling and storage: DEG is harmful if swallowed (H302) and may cause damage to the kidneys through prolonged or repeated exposure if swallowed (H373). It is not regulated as dangerous goods for road or sea transport. It has a high flash point and low vapour pressure; store it in closed carbon-steel or stainless tanks or drums, dry and away from strong oxidisers and acids, because it absorbs water from the air. Wear chemical gloves and goggles, and label every container so it cannot be mistaken for glycerine. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis giving purity, water content and colour, and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, 2–3 days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the quantity, pack type, end use and delivery site.

faqs.question: What is the difference between DEG and MEG or TEG?
faqs.answer: DEG sits between MEG and TEG in the ethylene glycol series. MEG is the antifreeze and PET feedstock; TEG is the standard gas-dehydration desiccant; DEG serves polyester resins, plasticisers and dehydration blend make-up, with lower volatility than MEG at lower cost than TEG. For chilled-water antifreeze use MEG or propylene glycol — not DEG.

faqs.question: Is DEG safe for food or pharmaceutical use?
faqs.answer: No. Diethylene glycol is toxic if ingested and must never be used in food, beverage, pharmaceutical or personal-care products. For those applications we supply USP/EP-grade propylene glycol (E1520). DEG is sold for industrial use only, with end-use declarations where required.

title: TEG (Triethylene Glycol)
description: High-purity triethylene glycol for natural gas dehydration.

details.longDescription:
Triethylene glycol (TEG, C6H14O4, CAS 112-27-6) is a clear, colourless, viscous and strongly hygroscopic liquid supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99% minimum purity, boiling point 285 °C and specific gravity 1.125 at 20 °C, in drums, 1,000 L IBCs, ISO tanks and bulk from stock in Muscat, for gas plants and industrial users across Oman and the GCC.

Gas dehydration is the main use. In a glycol contactor, lean TEG absorbs water vapour from natural gas so the gas leaves dry enough to meet pipeline and LNG specifications and will not form hydrates or free water downstream; the rich glycol is then regenerated by boiling off the water in a reboiler and recycled. TEG is preferred over DEG and MEG for this duty because its high boiling point lets it be regenerated to 98.5–99% purity at reboiler temperatures around 200 °C with low vapour losses, and stripping gas raises lean purity further where a deeper dew point is needed. Keep the reboiler below about 204 °C, as TEG begins to decompose near 207 °C, keep oxygen out of the system, and watch pH, which falls as degradation acids build up; plant operators top up losses with make-up TEG. The glycol comparison guide linked on this page sets out TEG, DEG and MEG side by side.

Other uses: a humectant and plasticiser in resins, inks, adhesives and cellulose films; a solvent and coupling agent; a component of hydraulic and heat-transfer fluids; an intermediate for esters and polyester resins; and the base fluid of some fog and haze machines.

Handling and storage: TEG is low in toxicity, combustible only at high temperature, and not regulated for transport. Its main storage issue is water pickup, which spoils it for dehydration duty, so keep drums tightly closed and tanks under a dry gas blanket; store in carbon-steel or stainless tanks. Wear gloves and safety glasses. Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis giving purity, water content and colour, a technical data sheet and a safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, 2–3 days to Salalah and Duqm, to the interior gas plants by arrangement, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the volume, pack type and delivery schedule.

faqs.question: What is TEG and how is it used for natural gas dehydration in Oman?
faqs.answer: Triethylene glycol (TEG, CAS 112-27-6) is a high-boiling-point hygroscopic liquid used as the primary dehydration solvent in gas processing plants throughout Oman. Natural gas from Oman's reservoirs contains water vapour that must be removed before export or LNG processing to prevent pipeline corrosion, hydrate formation, and to meet gas sales specifications (typically below 7 lb/MMSCF or 112 mg/Nm³ water content). In a TEG contactor unit, wet gas flows counter-current to lean TEG (99.5%+ purity) in an absorption column, where TEG absorbs the water vapour. The water-rich ("rich") TEG is then regenerated by heating to 190–205°C in a reboiler, which boils off the absorbed water as steam, restoring lean TEG purity for recirculation. TEG is preferred over MEG and DEG for gas plant dehydration because of its lower vapour pressure (meaning lower TEG losses in the gas stream) and its ability to achieve deeper dew point depressions. Global Chemicals LLC supplies technical-grade TEG for Oman's gas processing operations.

faqs.question: What causes TEG degradation in gas plant regenerators in Oman?
faqs.answer: TEG degradation in Oman gas plant regenerators occurs through several mechanisms. Thermal degradation begins at reboiler temperatures above 207°C, producing 1,4-dioxane, diethylene glycol, and polyglycol oligomers that accumulate as dark-coloured solids reducing TEG purity and absorption capacity. Oxidative degradation occurs when air ingresses into the system — oxygen reacts with TEG at elevated temperatures to form glycolic acid, oxalic acid, and other acidic degradation products that lower pH, accelerate corrosion, and promote foaming. pH control below 6.0 indicates acid degradation requiring base injection (sodium hydroxide, borax) and activated carbon filtration to remove degradation products. Contaminant accumulation from produced water (methanol, heavy hydrocarbons, amines, corrosion inhibitors) also accelerates TEG deterioration. In Oman's gas plants, TEG quality is monitored monthly by pH, colour, purity, and specific gravity testing. Reclaimer units and activated carbon filters significantly extend TEG service life. Global Chemicals LLC supplies fresh make-up TEG and regeneration chemicals for Oman gas operations.

title: Propylene Glycol (USP/Industrial)
description: Food-grade and industrial propylene glycol for various applications.

details.longDescription:
Propylene glycol (1,2-propanediol, PG, MPG, C3H8O2, CAS 57-55-6) is the low-toxicity glycol: a clear, colourless, viscous liquid with a boiling point of 188 °C and specific gravity 1.036, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in USP pharmaceutical grade at 99.5% minimum and in technical grade, in 200 L drums, 1,000 L IBCs and bulk from stock in Muscat and Rusayl Industrial Area. It does most of what ethylene glycol does, lowering freezing points, raising boiling points, carrying heat, holding moisture and dissolving flavours and actives, without ethylene glycol's toxicity, which is why the food and pharmaceutical grades hold GRAS status and go wherever a leak could reach people, food or animals.

USP grade. Food and beverage plants run 30–50% propylene glycol solutions as the secondary coolant in breweries, dairies, ice-cream and juice lines and cold stores, so a heat-exchanger leak is harmless; pharmaceutical makers use it as a solvent and carrier in oral, topical and injectable preparations; cosmetics and personal-care formulators as a humectant and solvent in creams, deodorants, toothpaste and hair products; the food industry as a humectant, flavour carrier and the additive E1520; feed mills as an energy supplement and preservative (never in cat food, where it is prohibited); and e-liquid, fragrance and theatrical-fog producers as the base fluid. Every USP delivery carries the pharmacopoeial certificate of analysis.

Technical grade. The same molecule in industrial purity serves as the heat-transfer and antifreeze fluid in HVAC and solar circuits where the glycol is inhibited and need not be food-safe, in aircraft and runway de-icing fluids, in hydraulic and brake fluids, as the diol of unsaturated polyester resins and alkyds, and as a plasticiser and solvent in paints and inks. The glycols guide linked on this page compares it with monoethylene and butylene glycol.

Handling and storage: propylene glycol is combustible with a flash point near 99 °C, not flammable at ambient temperature, low in toxicity and readily biodegradable; it is hygroscopic, so keep drums closed and dry, store under cover in carbon-steel, stainless or HDPE, and wear gloves and safety glasses. It is not regulated for transport. A technical data sheet and GHS safety data sheet ship with every delivery.

Delivery is same day within Muscat and Rusayl, next day to Sohar, 2–3 days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain, with a GCC certificate of origin where the material is GCC-made. Request a quote with the grade, pack type and monthly volume.

faqs.question: What is the difference between propylene glycol and ethylene glycol for Oman industrial use?
faqs.answer: Propylene glycol (PG, 1,2-propanediol, CAS 57-55-6) and ethylene glycol (MEG, 1,2-ethanediol) are both diols widely used as antifreeze, coolants, and industrial solvents, but differ critically in toxicity. Ethylene glycol is toxic (LD50 4,700 mg/kg in rats), metabolised to oxalic acid which causes kidney failure; propylene glycol is Generally Recognised As Safe (GRAS) by the FDA for use in food, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. This toxicity difference makes propylene glycol the mandatory choice for food processing refrigeration systems, brewery chilling loops, pharmaceutical manufacturing coolants, and any application where human contact is possible. In performance, both provide similar freeze protection and boiling point elevation at equivalent concentrations, but PG is slightly more viscous than MEG, requiring higher pump power in cold conditions. Cost: propylene glycol is typically 30–60% more expensive than MEG. For Oman industrial applications with no food contact risk (HVAC, process cooling, oilfield), MEG remains the standard. Global Chemicals LLC supplies both grades with documentation for food and industrial applications.
